title: Short AVGO — AI Capex Plateau Repricing Second Phase; Guidance Ceiling Not a Floor
entry: Short $408–425 on a relief bounce from the two-session 15% selloff. Best entry: any intraday rip to $415–425 that stalls with declining volume. Do not short below $405 into potential panic-driven demand. Scale: 60% on the first bounce attempt, 40% add at $418–425 if the bounce fails on volume at higher levels.
stop_loss: $445 daily close (~6.8% above entry midpoint $416.50) — implies institutional buyers treated the June 4 intraday recovery as definitive, the $435 level was a true floor not a false floor, and the market is repricing the stock back toward its pre-earnings base above $460.
targets: $385 — first institutional demand band; the briefing's explicit 'better entry' zone for long investors ($380–400); sell-side models begin cutting estimates on flat FY2027 guide; -7.6% from entry midpoint

$355 — base case fair value after full guidance-plateau repricing; Q3 FY2026 AI guide of $16B beats but the sequential growth rate disappointment becomes consensus; AVGO trades at 28x forward earnings on the new lower trajectory; -14.8%

$305 — Blue sky short: Q3 FY2026 AI revenue guide proves to be a ceiling, not a floor; hyperscaler custom-ASIC orders slow as Google/Apple internalize chip design; SPCX $75B capital drain + OpenAI IPO ($100B+ target, September 2026) compete for the same institutional AI-semiconductor allocation; -26.8%
catalyst: Broadcom Q2 FY2026 earnings (reported June 3 after close): FY2027 AI semiconductor revenue guidance left unchanged at '>$100B' despite +143% YoY in Q2 AI revenue. Q3 FY2026 AI revenue guide of $16B — while +200% YoY — implies sequential growth of only 48% vs. Q2's $10.8B run-rate, short of the $18–20B that the most aggressive buy-side models had penciled in. Stock declined from $479.23 to $418.91 on the June 4 close despite an intraday reversal attempt. AVGO's long-cycle institutional selling pattern (typical for guidance-plateau repricing in semiconductor names) is now in its second phase.
thesis:
Broadcom's FY2027 AI semiconductor revenue guidance at '>$100B' was left unchanged after reporting $10.8B for Q2 FY2026 — a floor that was set months ago, not a new commitment. The market had priced in a guidance raise to $120–130B from the most aggressive models: when management declined to raise the ceiling, despite reporting +143% YoY AI revenue in Q2, it confirmed that the FY2027 number represents a hard planning horizon, not a conservative base that will be beat by its normal margin. The two-session 15% decline from $479 to $418 reflects this repricing, and it is unlikely to be complete after just two sessions.

Institutional selling patterns in guidance-plateau situations follow a well-documented arc. Phase 1 (June 3-4) is the initial gap-down and the dip-buyer response — the same-day recovery on June 4 from $413 to $479 followed by the June 4 close at $418.91 is exactly this pattern: real institutional buyers at $413-420, real institutional sellers at $470-479, equilibrium established near $418. Phase 2 (the current window) is where portfolio managers who set hard 'three consecutive sessions above $440' confirmation criteria observe the June 4 close failure and begin systematic reduction. Phase 2 selling is quieter, spread over 10-20 trading days, and typically ends when a new demand level is established — the briefing explicitly identifies $380–400 as the institutional re-entry level, implying that Phase 2 ends in the $380-400 zone, not where we are today.

The hyperscaler capex context supports a measured short. Google guided for 'disciplined' H2 2026 spending after Q1 capex of $17.4B. Meta left 2026 AI capex guidance unchanged at $38–40B — notable because in prior quarters guidance was raised quarter-over-quarter. AWS H2 capex is guided flat at $18–20B. The plateau that spooked AVGO's stock is consistent with hyperscaler infrastructure cycles entering a consolidation phase after two years of frenzied expansion. AVGO's $16B Q3 AI guide implies $21–22B in Q4 FY2026 AI revenue to hit the $56B full-year target — a 30–35% sequential quarterly increase that would be unprecedented in AVGO's history and is more likely to require another guidance adjustment later in the year.

The position is sized at 3% and conviction is explicitly low — this is an asymmetric contrarian short on a structurally strong company temporarily in a guidance-plateau repricing cycle. The stop at $445 is above the $440 failed confirmation level and represents the point at which the Phase 2 selling thesis is structurally invalidated. The tight stop reflects that AVGO is not a broken company — it is the dominant custom AI silicon provider — and the short is a trade on near-term repricing momentum, not a fundamental short. Position exits in full if the stock closes above $445 on any session.
bull_case: Q3 FY2026 AI revenue beats the $16B guide by 15–20% (prints $18.5–19.5B) as management's conservative guidance philosophy, not demand deceleration, explains the plateau. Buy-side models revise FY2027 estimates higher; sell-side upgrades flow in. The guidance-plateau narrative reverses in 3-4 weeks and AVGO re-rates toward $460–480. Stop triggered at $445.
bear_case: Q3 FY2026 AI revenue misses the $16B guide — hyperscaler custom-ASIC orders slowed more than management indicated, and the Q4 FY2026 ask of $21–22B sequential growth is formally revised downward. AVGO guides Q4 FY2026 AI revenue at $17–18B, cutting the full-year $56B guide to $51–53B. Stock falls to $340–360, overshooting the $305 Target 3 on a guidance cut.
invalidation: $445 daily close, OR Broadcom pre-announces Q3 AI revenue tracking materially above $16B before the formal earnings date, OR any hyperscaler announces expansion of custom ASIC commitments with Broadcom specifically (Apple M-series AI ASIC acceleration, Google TPU v6 order increase, Meta Artemis chip production ramp).
